tasks.short: Explain safety procedures and demonstrate equipment

steps.what: Read the safety procedures for this recreational activity.
Explain the safety procedures to the participants.
Demonstrate use of the materials and equipment.
Notice which participant needs the technique shown again.

tasks.design: She reads the safety procedure in {DOCS}, explains those procedures to the participants, and demonstrates the materials and equipment herself. Nothing speaks for her and nothing scores a participant.
tasks.previous_blocker: The participant has to see the technique and the equipment. A written procedure does not show it.
tasks.enabler_now: A safety procedure can sit in a document store. That does not shorten the explanation or the demonstration.
tasks.still_hard: She has to watch each person with the equipment and show the technique again when it is wrong.
tasks.human_edge: She sees who is holding the equipment wrong and changes the demonstration in the moment.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in how she explains the procedures or demonstrates the equipment.

reach.task: Demonstrate a movement to a class
reach.learn: The cue that keeps a beginner on the safe version of the movement

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: explaining a safety procedure and demonstrating equipment stay with the person, because the participant has to see the technique. This is not a measured saving.
Annex III point 3 covers assignment to education and evaluating learning outcomes. This design does not assign a participant to education and does not score a learning outcome.
A decision based solely on automated processing needs a basis under GDPR article 22. This design does not decide by machine who may take part.

assumptions: The safety procedure is a document she already reads. No machine step consumes a structured field.
No system is built for this task, so ongoing upkeep is zero.
Explaining and demonstrating stay at full time. Nothing in the design shortens those steps.
unknowns: Whether participants include children, which would change consent for any record of the session. This design keeps no such record.
research_questions: Where is the safety procedure kept for each recreational activity?

incremental.description: No system is built, so there is no ongoing upkeep for this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: She still reads the procedure, explains it, and demonstrates the equipment. No step is shortened, so the saving is zero on a week of ordinary sessions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Direct aquatics, gymnastics or performing-arts events

steps.what: Read the plan for this aquatics or gymnastics event.
Check the equipment set for this special event.
Direct participants through the aquatics or gymnastics event.
Decide when this aquatics or gymnastics activity must stop.
Tell the group the next part of the performing event.

tasks.design: She reads the event plan in {DOCS}, checks the equipment, and directs the aquatics, gymnastics or performing-arts event herself, including the decision to stop. No system directs the group and nothing fills a run sheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: The event is live. Stopping it depends on what she sees in the moment.
tasks.enabler_now: An event plan can sit in a document store. That does not shorten directing the event.
tasks.still_hard: She has to direct the group and stop the activity when the water, the equipment or the group is unsafe.
tasks.human_edge: She stops the activity when she sees that the group or the setup is unsafe.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in how she directs the event or decides that it must stop.

reach.task: Set out equipment before an event
reach.learn: Which setup the attendant treats as ready before the event starts

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: directing an aquatics, gymnastics or performing-arts event stays with the person, because the group has to be led in the room. This is not a measured saving.
A decision based solely on automated processing needs a basis under GDPR article 22. This design does not decide by machine when an event stops.

assumptions: The event plan is a document she already reads. The equipment check is in person. No machine step consumes a structured field.
No system is built for this task, so ongoing upkeep is zero.
Directing, the stop decision and telling the group the next part stay at full time.
unknowns: Whether aquatics has a separate lifeguard on duty. This design does not move the stop decision.
research_questions: Where is the plan for an aquatics or gymnastics event kept?

incremental.description: No system is built, so there is no ongoing upkeep for this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: She still checks the setup, directs the event and decides when it stops. No step is shortened, so the saving is zero on a week of ordinary events.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Train staff members and assign their duties

steps.what: List personnel she will supervise before assigning duties.
Decide which duties each staff member will take.
Tell that staff member the duty she assigned.
Train staff members on the activity for those duties.
Write the duties she assigned for those staff members.

tasks.design: The staff roster in {OTHER} lists personnel only when staff name and shift start are already stored. She still decides each duty, tells the staff member, trains them, and writes the duties herself. A blank name is left off the list and she asks who is in. The list does not assign a duty and does not alert anyone.
tasks.previous_blocker: The rota and the duty were separate papers, and assigning the duty depends on the person in front of her.
tasks.enabler_now: A roster that already stores staff name and shift start can be listed, so she does not re-read the sheet for names that are filled.
tasks.still_hard: Training and the choice of duty stay with her. A blank roster name is left off and she asks in the room.
tasks.human_edge: She changes the duty when the person in front of her is not ready for that activity, and she trains them herself.
tasks.altitude: She still decides the duty and trains in the room. She stops re-reading the rota when staff name and shift start are filled.

reach.task: Follow the duty she was given
reach.learn: Which part of the duty the assistant still needs shown

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a list can show staff name and shift start that a roster already stores. Training and the duty decision stay with the person. This is not a measured saving.

An app that time-stamps each staff action can monitor performance and needs consent under the Dutch works-council rule on staff monitoring. This list stores staff name and shift start for the day. It does not time-stamp the training. Whether a works council exists is unknown, and other countries differ.
A decision based solely on automated processing needs a basis under GDPR article 22. This design does not decide by machine who takes a duty.

assumptions: The weekly roster is produced outside this task by the person who sets the rota. It stores staff name and shift start. A blank name is omitted from the list, and she asks who is in. That ask stays in the tell step at full time. The capture of those roster fields is not counted as time saved here.
She writes the duty note herself on paper. Nothing else copies it onto a board, sends it, or alerts the staff member.
The list is a read of names already stored. It is not a score of how fast someone trained. Upkeep is 0.3 hours per 100 hours of this task, for a roster row whose name or shift start is wrong.
unknowns: Whether a works council exists, and whether national rules treat a duty list as monitoring. The digest names the Dutch works-council rule.
research_questions: Does the weekly rota store staff name and shift start before the shift starts?

incremental.description: Correct a roster row whose staff name or shift start is wrong, per 100 hours of this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a week where staff name and shift start are filled, she skips re-reading the rota. On a week of blank names she asks in the room and the saving is near zero. Training and the duty decision are not shortened. The figure is not a published admin percentage.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Evaluate recreation areas, facilities and services

steps.what: Show booked count and capacity for each recreation session.
Walk the recreation areas and notice the facilities.
Ask participants whether these recreation services worked.
Decide whether these facilities produced the desired results.
Write the evaluation of these recreation services.

tasks.design: The booking record in {OTHER} shows booked count against capacity for a recreation session only when session, date, booked count and capacity are already stored. She still walks the areas, asks participants, decides whether the facilities produced the desired results, and writes the evaluation herself in {DOCS}. A blank count is left off. The list does not send an alert.
tasks.previous_blocker: Headcount sat in a booking book, and whether the service worked depends on the walk and on what participants say.
tasks.enabler_now: A booking record that already stores session, date, booked count and capacity can be listed, so she does not tally those counts by hand.
tasks.still_hard: The walk and the judgement of results stay with her. A blank count is left off and she counts during the walk.
tasks.human_edge: She judges the facility from what she sees and from what participants say, not from the headcount alone.
tasks.altitude: She still walks the facility and decides the result. She stops tallying the register when booked count and capacity are filled.

reach.task: Decide a repair from the facility evaluation
reach.learn: Which result the supervisor treats as enough to book a repair

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a list can show a booked count and a capacity that a booking record already stores. The walk and the judgement stay with the person. This is not a measured saving.
Annex III point 3 covers assignment to education and evaluating learning outcomes. This evaluation is of the facility and the service. It does not score a participant's learning.
A decision based solely on automated processing needs a basis under GDPR article 22. This design does not decide by machine whether a service produced the desired result.

assumptions: The booking record is produced outside this task by the person who takes the booking. It stores session, date, booked count and capacity. A blank count is omitted. She counts during the walk, which stays at full time. The capture of those booking fields is not counted as time saved here.
She writes the evaluation herself in the document store. Nothing else files it, and the list does not send an alert.
Upkeep is 0.3 hours per 100 hours of this task, for a booked count she finds wrong and corrects herself. The walk, the questions and the decision stay at full time.
unknowns: Whether the booking record stores booked count and capacity as separate fields for each session.
research_questions: Does the booking record store booked count and capacity as separate fields for each session?

incremental.description: Correct a booked count she finds wrong during the walk, per 100 hours of this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a week where booked count and capacity are filled, she skips tallying the register. On a week of blank counts, or a result that is about the room rather than headcount, the saving is near zero. The walk and the decision are not shortened. The figure is not a published admin percentage.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Her week is still demonstrations, live events, staff training and walks through the facility. She stops re-reading the rota when staff name and shift start are filled, and she stops tallying a register when booked count and capacity are filled.
skills_to_grow: Demonstrate a technique while watching who has not followed the safety procedure
Stop an aquatics or gymnastics event when the group is unsafe
Assign a duty from the person in front of her, not from the roster alone
Judge a facility from the walk, not from the booked count
role.ambitious_version: She still explains, directs, trains and walks the floor. A rota row with a blank name is left off the list, and a session with a blank booked count is left off too.
